description: AWS Network Firewall Suricata Content Keywords
note: This file contains keywords verified to work with AWS Network Firewall. Users can add new keywords as AWS/Suricata adds features.

keywords.name: flow
keywords.description: Match on direction and state of the flow. Supports multiple comma-separated values
notes: to_server = match packets from client to server
to_client = match packets from server to client
from_client = same as to_server
from_server = same as to_client
established = match on established connections
not_established = match on packets not part of established connection
stateless = match packets part of a flow regardless of connection state
only_stream = match on reassembled stream packets
no_stream = match on packets not reassembled by stream engine
only_frag = match on reassembled fragment packets
no_frag = match on packets not reassembled from fragments

keywords.name: content
keywords.description: Match specific content in payload. Can be negated with ! prefix

keywords.name: msg
keywords.description: Rule message/description that appears in logs

keywords.name: sid
keywords.description: Rule signature ID (1-999999999)

keywords.name: rev
keywords.description: Rule revision number (1 or greater)

keywords.name: tls.sni
keywords.description: Match TLS Server Name Indication (SNI) field

keywords.name: tls.cert_issuer
keywords.description: Match TLS/SSL certificate Issuer field. Sticky buffer for certificate issuer DN

keywords.name: http.host

forbidden_modifier_reasons.nocase: http.host buffer is automatically normalized to lowercase

keywords.description: Match HTTP host header. Buffer is automatically normalized to lowercase — do NOT use nocase modifier.
notes: Buffer is normalized to lowercase — nocase is redundant and will cause an error
Use endswith for suffix matching (e.g., .example.com)
Use dotprefix for subdomain wildcard matching

keywords.name: http.uri
keywords.description: Match HTTP URI path

keywords.name: http.method
keywords.description: Match HTTP method

keywords.name: http.header_names
keywords.description: Match on HTTP header names for presence, absence, or order checking. Starts with CRLF and ends with extra CRLF
notes: Use flow:to_server for request headers, flow:to_client for response headers
Buffer starts with \r\n and ends with extra \r\n
Format: |0d 0a|HeaderName|0d 0a|
Useful for header presence/absence checking
Can detect header order with distance modifier
Negation (!) checks for header absence

keywords.name: http.request_header
keywords.description: Match on HTTP request header name and value pair. Works with both HTTP/1 and HTTP/2. Use |3a 20| (colon space) to separate header name from value
notes: Works with HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 traffic
For HTTP/2, matches pseudo-headers like :authority, :method, :path
Use |3a 20| hex bytes for the colon-space separator between header name and value

keywords.name: http2.header_name
keywords.description: Match on HTTP/2 header name. Used for matching HTTP/2 pseudo-headers such as authority, method, path. Requires TLS inspection for decrypted HTTP/2 traffic
notes: Only works with HTTP/2 protocol traffic
Requires TLS inspection to decrypt HTTP/2
Use with http2 protocol in rule header

keywords.name: dns.query
keywords.description: Match DNS query name

keywords.name: ja3.hash
keywords.description: Match JA3 TLS client fingerprint hash

keywords.name: ja3s.hash
keywords.description: Match JA3S TLS server fingerprint hash

keywords.name: ja4.hash
keywords.description: Match JA4 TLS fingerprint hash (newer version)

keywords.name: ssl_state
keywords.description: Match on SSL/TLS handshake state. Multiple states can be specified with | (OR)

keywords.name: ssl_version
keywords.description: Match version of SSL/TLS record. Multiple versions can be specified with commas to match any of the listed versions.
notes: Matches the SSL/TLS record version, not negotiated version
Multiple versions can be comma-separated (matches if ANY listed version is seen)
Negation (!) is NOT supported in AWS Network Firewall
To block old versions: use alert/drop with ssl_version:tls1.0,tls1.1 to match deprecated traffic

keywords.name: app-layer-protocol
keywords.description: Match on application layer protocol. Can be negated with ! prefix

keywords.name: geoip
keywords.description: Match on GeoIP country code. Direction can be 'src', 'dst', 'any' (OR logic), or 'both' (AND logic). Supports multiple country codes and negation with ! prefix. Supports IPv4 and IPv6.
notes: src = match source IP only
dst = match destination IP only
any = match if source OR destination matches (OR logic)
both = match if source AND destination match (AND logic)
Supports multiple comma-separated country codes
Negation (!) must prefix each country code individually (e.g., !US,!GB)
Cannot be combined with app-layer keywords (tls.sni, http.*, dns.query, etc.) in the same rule
Uses MaxMind GeoIP database for IP-to-country lookups
IP must have a location in MaxMind's database to match — anycast IPs will not match
Network Firewall only allows valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes
Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 (expanded from base Suricata)

keywords.name: metadata
keywords.description: Add metadata tags to the rule for organizational purposes

keywords.name: flowbits
keywords.description: Set or check flow-based state tracking

keywords.name: noalert
keywords.description: Suppress alert generation (useful with flowbits for tracking without alerting)

keywords.name: ip_proto
keywords.description: Match on IP protocol (name or number 0-255). Can be negated with ! prefix

keywords.name: dotprefix
keywords.description: Match domain and all subdomains. Must be placed before 'content' and domain must include leading dot

keywords.name: startswith
keywords.description: Content modifier - match at the beginning of the buffer

keywords.name: endswith
keywords.description: Content modifier - match at the end of the buffer

keywords.name: nocase
keywords.description: Content modifier - case-insensitive matching

keywords.name: offset
keywords.description: Content modifier - number of bytes to skip before starting pattern match

keywords.name: depth
keywords.description: Content modifier - how far into the buffer to search

keywords.name: distance
keywords.description: Content modifier - bytes to skip after previous match before starting next match

keywords.name: within
keywords.description: Content modifier - search within specified bytes after previous match

keywords.name: alert
keywords.description: Force alert even on pass rules (shows verdict as 'alert' instead of 'pass')
keywords.example: pass tls $HOME_NET any -> any any (alert; tls.sni; content:"example.com"; sid:100; rev:1;)

keywords.name: isdataat
keywords.description: Check if data exists at specified position in payload

keywords.name: pcre
keywords.description: Perl Compatible Regular Expression pattern matching

keywords.name: byte_test
keywords.description: Test byte values at specific offset

keywords.name: byte_jump
keywords.description: Jump forward in payload based on byte value

keywords.name: dsize
keywords.description: Match on payload data size

keywords.name: flags
keywords.description: Match TCP flags. Supports multiple flags (e.g., SA, FPU), modifiers (+/*!/=), and optional mask (e.g., S,CE)
notes: F=FIN, S=SYN, R=RST, P=PSH, A=ACK, U=URG, C=CWR, E=ECE, 0=No flags
+ = match all specified bits plus any others
* = match if any specified bits are set
! = match if bits are not set
= = match only specified bits and no others
Mask: S,CE checks for SYN flag regardless of CWR/ECE bits

keywords.name: threshold
keywords.description: Rate limiting and thresholds for alerts. Functional in AWS Network Firewall but locally significant per firewall instance.
keywords.example: threshold:type limit, track by_src, count 1, seconds 60
examples: threshold:type limit, track by_src, count 1, seconds 60;
threshold:type threshold, track by_dst, count 5, seconds 300;
threshold:type both, track by_src, count 10, seconds 60;
notes: Types: limit (alert on first N), threshold (alert every Nth), both (limit + suppress after)
Track: by_src or by_dst
The threshold keyword is locally significant in AWS Network Firewall
Network Firewall runs multiple instances behind a load balancer
Each instance tracks its own threshold counter independently
Actual threshold behavior may be multiplied by the number of instances
Best used for rate limiting rather than exact count enforcement

keywords.name: classtype
keywords.description: Classify rule for priority assignment

keywords.name: priority
keywords.description: Set rule priority (1=highest, 4=lowest)

keywords.name: reference
keywords.description: External reference for the rule

keywords.name: xbits
keywords.unsupported_reason: requires undocumented rule hook — use flowbits instead
keywords.description: Transaction-level bit tracking. Listed as partially supported in AWS Network Firewall documentation but may require explicit rule hooks not documented publicly. Consider using flowbits instead for reliable cross-rule state tracking.
notes: track ip_src, ip_dst, and ip_pair are explicitly NOT supported
track tx may require an explicit rule hook (undocumented requirement)
Consider using flowbits for reliable state tracking in AWS Network Firewall
Only 'set' and 'isset' operations are supported (not unset, isnotset, toggle)

keywords.name: aws_url_category
keywords.description: Match traffic based on AWS-maintained URL categories. Only supports HTTP protocol. Supports comma-separated categories. For HTTPS traffic, requires TLS inspection/decryption to be effective. Cannot be combined with geoip in same rule.
notes: Only supports HTTP protocol (use protocol http)
Requires TLS inspection for HTTPS traffic effectiveness
Cannot be combined with geoip filtering
Category database automatically maintained by AWS
Evaluates complete URL path (30 recursive lookups)
Falls back to domain-level evaluation (10 subdomain lookups)
Single URL may map to multiple categories

keywords.name: aws_domain_category
keywords.description: Match traffic based on AWS-maintained domain categories. Supports TLS and HTTP protocols. Supports comma-separated categories. Works without TLS inspection. Cannot be combined with geoip in same rule.
examples: aws_domain_category:Adult and Mature Content,Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning;
notes: Supports TLS and HTTP protocols
For TLS: inspects SNI field (works without TLS decryption)
For HTTP: inspects host header
Cannot be combined with geoip filtering
Category database automatically maintained by AWS
Domain-level evaluation only (10 subdomain lookups)
More effective with TLS inspection but functions without it
Single domain may map to multiple categories

keywords.name: http.request_body
keywords.description: Match on HTTP request body (POST data). Sticky buffer for the normalized request body.

keywords.name: http.response_body
keywords.description: Match on HTTP response body content. Sticky buffer for the normalized response body.

keywords.name: http.user_agent
keywords.description: Match on HTTP User-Agent header value. Sticky buffer for the User-Agent field.

keywords.name: http.content_type
keywords.description: Match on HTTP Content-Type header value. Sticky buffer for the Content-Type field.

keywords.name: http.stat_code
keywords.description: Match on HTTP response status code. Sticky buffer for the response status code.

keywords.name: http.stat_msg
keywords.description: Match on HTTP response status message. Sticky buffer for the response status message.

keywords.name: fast_pattern
keywords.description: Content modifier that forces this content match to be used as the fast pattern matcher. Helps Suricata optimize rule matching by selecting this pattern for the multi-pattern matcher.
notes: Should be applied to the most unique/rare content match in a rule
Only one content match per rule can have fast_pattern
Improves rule performance by guiding the multi-pattern matcher

keywords.name: bsize
keywords.description: Match on the size of the current sticky buffer. Similar to dsize but works on any sticky buffer (http.host, http.uri, etc.).
notes: Operators: < (less than), > (greater than), = (equal), or no operator for exact match
Works on the preceding sticky buffer (http.host, http.uri, http.header_names, etc.)

keywords.name: tls.fingerprint
keywords.description: Match TLS/SSL certificate SHA1 fingerprint. Format is colon-separated hex (XX:YY:ZZ:...). Not a sticky buffer — takes the value directly after colon.
notes: Fingerprint is the SHA1 hash of the DER-encoded certificate
Format: colon-separated hex bytes in quotes
NOT a sticky buffer — use tls.fingerprint:"value" directly (not tls.fingerprint; content:"value")
Use with flow:to_client,established to match server certificate
Can be negated with ! prefix before the quoted value

keywords.name: tls.cert_subject
keywords.description: Match TLS/SSL certificate Subject field (Distinguished Name). Sticky buffer for certificate subject DN.
notes: Matches against the Subject Distinguished Name of the certificate
Use isdataat:!1,relative for exact match (no trailing data)
Common fields: CN (Common Name), O (Organization), OU (Organizational Unit)
Use with flow:to_client,established to match server certificate

keywords.name: flowint
keywords.description: Flow integer variables for counting and tracking within a flow. Allows arithmetic and comparison operations on per-flow integer counters.
notes: Variables are per-flow (reset when flow ends)
Supports arithmetic: + (add), - (subtract), = (set)
Supports comparison: >, <, >=, <=, ==, !=
isset/isnotset check if variable has been initialized
Useful for detecting brute force or repeated patterns within a connection

keywords.name: stream_size
keywords.description: Match on the size of the stream in a given direction. Checks accumulated bytes in the stream.
notes: client = bytes from client to server
server = bytes from server to client
both = combined bytes in both directions
either = bytes in either direction (whichever is larger)

keywords.name: flow.age
keywords.unsupported_reason: not enabled in AWS Network Firewall suricata.yaml
keywords.description: Match on the age of the flow in seconds. Not supported in AWS Network Firewall.
